newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Switzerland's mountain of cash keeps on rising.
newsitem.headline: Switzerland's mountain of cash keeps on rising.

text.p: Assets of Switzerland's booming mutual funds jumped by nearly $7 billion in January, a new survey said on Thursday.

Swiss mutual fund statistician Bopp ISB said combined assets of public mutual funds set up by Swiss banks at home and abroad grew to 242.3 billion Swiss Francs ($167 billion) at the end of January from 232.4 billion at the end of 1996.

Swiss bankers say the mutual fund industry is expanding fast and many banks are seeking innovative niches in the market, where assets grew by 26 percent in 1996 with an average monthly net flow of 1.5 billion Swiss francs.
In a departure from their traditional image as bankers for the very rich, private banks are also aggressively selling funds to a smaller, more risk-averse pool of capital.

Nicholas Fliess of Intrag, the fund managing company for Union Bank of Switzerland, said the volume of assets in the bank's mutual funds family had soared by more than $1 billion in the first two months of this year.

"There's a lot of liquidity around. There's plenty of money waiting to be invested, a lot of people don't know what to do," he said. "If we continue like this, there'll be a lot of money in Swiss mutual funds by the end of the year."
UBS holds 26 percent of the market with combined assets of 61 billion Swiss francs under management in mutual funds.
The market leader is Swiss Bank Corporation with 30 percent of all industry assets worth 69 billion Swiss francs.
The Bopp ISB survey covers only public funds and not inhouse funds managed by private banks which do not publish any data on such assets worth many more billions of Swiss francs.
It also excludes foreign groups selling mutual funds in Switzerland such as Fidelity, Flemings, Citibank and Nomura.
Data on the total volume of assets managed is not published in Switzerland, a by-product of its culture of bank secrecy, and bank annual reports provide only scanty information.
Total private wealth under management in Switzerland is more than $1.8 trillion, according to a recent survey by Credit Suisse First Boston Bank.
